title.narrative: NIHR RIGHT 6: Affordable Cardiac Rehabilitation: An Outreach Inter-disciplinary Strategic Study (ACROSS)

description.narrative:
A UK and low- and middle-income country (LMIC) research partnership between the University of Glasgow and Ishrat Husain Pakistan Institute of Living and Learning that aims to develop an affordable home-based rehabilitation programme for people with long term conditions including heart disease and mental health conditions in Bangladesh, Pakistan and India.
Beginning in July 2025, the five-year project intends to build on existing research collaborations in South Asia to address the unmet needs of heart disease and mental health multimorbidity in South Asia. Home-based programmes provide an affordable model of delivery that can leverage a scalable increase in rehabilitation access in LMICs, a key strategic global goal of the World Health Organisation. The project aims to do this through the evaluation and implementation of a sustainable, cultural, and contextually appropriate model of home-based rehabilitation for people with multimorbidity that includes heart disease and a mental health disorder that is both affordable and scalable.

The award has five objectives:
1. To co-design with key stakeholders a culturally and contextually adapted, affordable home-based rehabilitation (‘ACROSS’) programme with low intensity inventions for depression and anxiety (Work Package 1). 2. To co-design ACROSS delivery training for health professionals to include a train-the-trainer programme to enable the cascade of training (Work Package 1). 3. To assess the feasibility and acceptability of the implementation of ACROSS programme as well as trial design and examine the parameters and processes of a full-scale trial, including recruitment, randomisation, and retention (Work Package 2). 4. To determine clinical effectiveness (hierarchical primary outcome of mortality, hospital admission, and health-related of quality life) of the ACROSS programme (Work Package 3). 5. To determine cost-effectiveness of ACROSS programme in terms of an incremental cost per quality adjusted life year (Work Package 3).
